pages.title: Prepare early, shed ahead, restore promptly
pages.text: When deep cold is forecast, line up extra plants, imports and conservation early. If supply is falling, shed a little ahead while keeping gas sites powered. Bring homes back as soon as reserves recover.

pages.title: Bring homes back in bigger steps
pages.text: Once reserves are comfortably above need, return homes in large steps. Do not wait for supply to stop wiggling. The bigger the spare power, the more homes come back each hour.

pages.title: Restore whenever the cushion holds
pages.text: Bring homes back in steady steps once reserves stay above a modest cushion and supply is not falling fast. Only cut ahead when reserves are truly thin.

strategy:
- Default prediction is 0% to +3%. Since the kept mid-band restore habit, every edit measured between -3.2% and +7.4%. Only predict below -5% when a failed storm shows a dark-hours pattern the kept habit cannot reach, and name that storm.
- Treat any edit that changes cut sizing, cut caps, damping, battery refill timing or restore triggers as interfering with the kept habit. Predict it as positive (worse), from +2% to +8%, or don't propose it. Night 11's damping and refill edits measured +7.4% and +2.6%.
- Never propose authority shifts or hard-limit caps or cushions. Their history is +15.8%, +7.4% and +0.1%. Gauge alarms and briefing tweaks measure about -3%, so predict -2% to -3% for those, never more.
- Look for mechanisms outside the cut and restore loop: which homes are targeted (critical loads, rotation fairness), cold-start or crew delays after the crunch, and supply-side switching. Cite the exact storm hours where homes stayed dark.
- For each idea, walk through the passed storm hour by hour. If the idea fires there at all, add +2% to the prediction. Report a range and pick its upper (worse) end as the point estimate.
- Propose fewer ideas, each a single new mechanism. Prefer one well-calibrated near-zero prediction over a hopeful big claim, because prediction error matters as much as finding a keeper.

sensors.description: coldest statewide temperature forecast in the next two days

sensors.name: supply_drop
sensors.description: how fast supply is changing over the last 3 hours (negative = falling)

rules.description: Deep cold forecast: commit extra units, schedule imports, ask for conservation before it arrives
Use demand response and batteries before cutting homes
Shed only when reserves are truly thin or supply is falling steeply, keeping gas facilities powered
Reserves above 5% and supply not falling fast: restore 2 GW of homes each hour
Large spare reserve while homes are dark: restore quickly in big steps

guardrails.description: Frequency emergency: control room cuts load immediately, keeping gas facilities powered
Whenever load is shed, gas facilities stay powered

alerts.description: Reserves getting thin: ask the AI

alerts.when: reserve_margin < 0.08 or supply_drop < 0 and reserve_margin < 0.12 or cold_ahead < -10 and hour == 18
